- Sterile pyuria (WBC 15–20/HPF) with negative nitrites and no documented bacteriuria  
- Microscopic hematuria (RBC 3–5/HPF)  
- Trace proteinuria  
- Positive leukocyte esterase  
- Elevated creatinine and BUN confirming AKI  
- Renal ultrasound: normal-sized kidneys, mild increased cortical echogenicity, no obstruction or structural lesions  
- Absence of RBC casts and dysmorphic RBCs — argues against glomerulonephritis  
- Normal C3/C4, negative ANA, negative c-/p-ANCA — reduces likelihood of immune-complex or vasculitic GN  

[GAPS]  
- No documented medication history (e.g., NSAIDs, PPIs, antibiotics used for sinusitis) — critical for establishing temporal association with AIN  
- No urine eosinophils (e.g., Hansel stain) — though low sensitivity/specificity, a positive result would support AIN  
- No serum IgE or peripheral eosinophilia reported — supportive (but not required) for drug-induced AIN  
- No renal biopsy — definitive confirmation is missing, though clinically unnecessary if response to withdrawal/steroids is observed  

[DIAGNOSIS]  
Acute Interstitial Nephritis
